calendar-invite.reveal_note: Nearly identical. The fake comes from googIe.com, with a capital I instead of the l in google, which is hard to see in most fonts, and it adds a sign-in step.
red_flags: A capital I, not an l
calendar-invite.what_you_can_do: Accept invites from your calendar app. If a sign-in appears, stop and check the address letter by letter.

invoice-approval.reveal_note: Everything reads professionally and the domain looks right at a glance. The tell is subtle: the fake domain has an added hyphen (rossum-supply.com vs rossumsupply.com), and the bank details changed without the phone confirmation finance policy requires.
red_flags: Bank details only in a file
invoice-approval.what_you_can_do: Phone the supplier on a number you already hold before changing any bank details.

it-vpn-certificate.subject_label: An IT email about your VPN certificate
it-vpn-certificate.reveal_note: The real email says the certificate renews by itself and no action is needed. The fake comes from meridianfreight-vpn.com, claims it has expired and links to a page to reinstall it.
it-vpn-certificate.what_you_can_do: IT never sends installers by email link. Raise a ticket on the Service Desk portal from your own bookmark.

oauth-consent.subject_label: A Microsoft account notice, on your phone
oauth-consent.reveal_note: Everything matches except one letter: the fake comes from microsft.com, missing an o. Real Microsoft emails tell you to review apps at account.microsoft.com yourself.
oauth-consent.what_you_can_do: Review connected apps by going to account.microsoft.com yourself.

qr-guest-wifi.reveal_note: The printed address is the same, which is what makes this hard. The fake is a sticker over the real code, and it asks guests for a work login. The QR really opens meridianfreight-guest.com.
red_flags: A sticker over the real code
Guests don't have a work login
qr-guest-wifi.what_you_can_do: Guest Wi-Fi never needs a work login. Ask reception for the password instead of scanning an unexpected code.

qr-paynow-counter.subject_label: A PayNow code at a cafe counter
qr-paynow-counter.reveal_note: Everything matches except two details: the fake is a sticker over the original, and its UEN differs from the one on the shop's receipts. Scanning pays a private account, not Kopi Corner.
red_flags: A sticker over the real code
qr-paynow-counter.what_you_can_do: Check the payee name in your banking app before you confirm. If it isn't the shop's name, don't pay.

singtel-ceo-office.subject_label: An email from the Group CEO Office
singtel-ceo-office.reveal_note: The real email only says thank you and needs no action. The fake comes from singtel-group.com and asks for your mobile number, the first step of a phone scam.
singtel-ceo-office.what_you_can_do: Executives' offices don't ask for your number by email. Check with your manager before you reply.

singtel-cyber-training.subject_label: A Singtel training reminder, on your phone
singtel-cyber-training.reveal_note: Both look the same on a phone. The real email tells you to use your own bookmark. The fake comes from singtel-learning.com and gives you a link that asks for your staff login.
singtel-cyber-training.what_you_can_do: Read the sender's address, then open the learning portal from your own bookmark.

sms-ceo-newnumber.reveal_note: The real message shows Daniel Koh because he is in your contacts. The fake arrives from an unknown number, claims it is Daniel's new one, and asks for a vague favour first.
red_flags: A vague ask to hook you
sms-ceo-newnumber.what_you_can_do: Call Daniel on the number you already have before you reply to a 'new number' message.
